intro: Continue the JWT key-rotation task in this repo (package `jwt-rotator`, ESM, tests run with `npm test` → `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"`). Here is where the previous agent left it.

sections.name: OBJECTIVE
lines: "We need to add key rotation support to our JWT verifier. Right now the `Verifier` takes a single public key. I want it to also accept an object mapping `kid` (key ID) strings to public keys." (developer)

sections.name: TASK SCOPE
lines: Update `Verifier` in `src/jwt.js` and its tests in `test/jwt.test.js`.
In `verify`, parse the token header (base64url-decoded JSON), extract `kid`, and verify the signature with the matching public key.
Keep backwards compatibility for a single key passed to the constructor.
Enforce strict rejection and exact error messages in key-map mode.

sections.name: REQUIREMENTS
lines: The `Verifier` constructor accepts either a single public key or an object mapping `kid` strings to public keys. (developer requirement)
`verify` parses the token header (base64url-decoded JSON), extracts `kid` and uses the matching public key to verify the signature. (developer requirement)
"For now", if someone passes a single string to the constructor, treat it as the default key for backwards compatibility. (developer requirement)
If the `Verifier` was built with a keys object and the token has no `kid` in its header, reject it immediately. "Don't try to fall back or guess the key." (developer requirement)
Downstream services rely on strict error messages, so the two messages below must match exactly. (developer requirement)

sections.name: EXACT VALUES
lines: Missing `kid` (with a keys object): `Token verification failed: Missing 'kid' in header` (developer requirement; this replaces the previous agent's earlier `'Missing key ID'`)

`kid` present but not in the keys object: `Token verification failed: Unknown key ID '<kid>'`, e.g. `Token verification failed: Unknown key ID 'key-9'` (developer requirement; this replaces the earlier `'Unknown key ID'`)
Existing messages, unchanged: `'Invalid token format'`, `'Invalid signature'`. Added by the previous agent: `'Invalid token header'`.
Error class: `TokenError` from `src/errors.js`.

sections.name: DECISIONS
sections.note: all made by the previous agent, not by the developer
lines: `isKeyMap`: a key map is a non-null object whose prototype is `Object.prototype` or `null`. Anything else (PEM string, `Buffer`, `KeyObject`) is treated as the single default key, and any `kid` in the token is ignored.
In map mode, `this.publicKey = null`. There is no fallback key and no looping over keys.
The map is copied in the constructor (`{ ...publicKey }`), so later changes to the original object have no effect.
Keys are looked up with `Object.hasOwn`, so `__proto__`, `constructor` and `toString` are rejected as unknown.
A `kid` that is not a string (e.g. `123`, `null`, `{}`) gets the "Missing 'kid'" message.
A header that is not valid JSON, or is not an object, throws `'Invalid token header'`.
`resolveKey(head64)` runs before any signature check.
The `kid` goes into the error message unfiltered, to keep the exact format.

sections.name: COMPLETED
sections.note: observed: git diff; the changes are unstaged and uncommitted on `main` @ fa6bfec "Initial state"
lines: `src/jwt.js`: added `isKeyMap`, a map-aware constructor and `resolveKey`. `verify` now uses the resolved key.
`test/jwt.test.js`: 8 new tests covering:
a single key with a `kid`
the map selecting the right key
the wrong key for a `kid`
an unknown `kid` (`'key-9'`)
inherited-property kids
a missing `kid` (signed by a key that *is* in the map, so a fallback would be caught)
an undecodable header
map copying (expects the `'key-2'` unknown message)
The tests compare the exact message strings.

sections.name: VERIFICATION
lines: Observed (turn 3, after the message change): `npm test 2>&1 | grep -E "^(not ok|# (pass|fail))"` → `# pass 12`, `# fail 0`.
Observed (turn 1): the full run showed 12/12 passing.

sections.name: UNKNOWN: BLOCKING
sections.note: needs a developer decision; do not choose yourself
lines: Whether to sanitize `kid` in the unknown-key error message. The `kid` comes from the token, so newlines could forge log lines and very long values could bloat logs. The previous agent proposed truncating long values and escaping control characters, and asked the developer "Should I add that?" No answer is established. This changes the strict error contract and is a security choice, so leave the current behavior as it is until the developer decides.

Compatibility risk the previous agent raised: Node also accepts keys in the form `{ key: pem, format: 'pem' }`. That is a plain object, so it would now be treated as a key map. Whether any callers pass keys this way is not established. It affects the public constructor interface, so raise it with the developer rather than changing `isKeyMap` on your own.

sections.name: UNKNOWN: NON-BLOCKING
lines: The developer's messages in the selected handoff context do not show a message for an invalid header. Keep `'Invalid token header'` as implemented and mention it in your report.

sections.name: NEXT STEP
lines: 1. Run `git diff` and `npm test` to confirm the working tree still matches the state above (12 pass, 0 fail).
2. If it does, the stated requirements are met. Report back to the developer and ask for the two blocking decisions: kid sanitization, and the `{ key, format }` key form.

3. If the developer approves sanitization, implement it so that normal `kid` values still produce exactly `Token verification failed: Unknown key ID '<kid>'`, add tests for newline and very long kids, and re-run `npm test`.
